notes.title: Patch 0.1.3 last improvements before the bigger Update
notes.notes:
General Updates
Updated Ingame Descriptions
All in-game texts have been revised to reflect the decision to release Everstead: Origins as an Early Access title following the Steam Next Fest feedback and number of wishlists.

Passive Gameplay Disclaimer
A new confirmation checkbox makes it clear from the start: Everstead is a passive village simulation. Too many players missed this core concept — now it’s unmistakably stated.
 Settler Improvements
Follow Function
You can now follow individual settlers via their detail panel — a great way to watch daily life, behavior, and personality up close.

Smarter Builders
Builders now fetch materials on their own, reducing early-game idle time and creating a smoother simulation flow.

notes.title: Patch 0.1.2 – Small Improvements Before the Big Leap
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Here’s a small but helpful update based on your feedback:

 Hammering sounds now come with subtle variations – no more identical clangs!

 Added a Reset Camera button to quickly refocus on your camp.

 Improved dropdown menu visuals for better readability and interaction.

 New controls menu: You can now check all inputs at any time.
[hr][/hr]
This will likely be the last patch during the Steam Next Fest – and for good reason:

The past two months have been an intense ride, and I’ll be taking a short creative break to recharge a bit. After that, I’ll fully commit to rebuilding the core settler system — making the game smarter, more reactive, and more immersive than ever before.




 Beaver Fever Games

notes.title: Hotfix V0.1.1
notes.notes:
Changelog:

 Fixed an issue where the demo didn’t end correctly after the first in-game day

 Resolved pathfinding problems near the creek where settlers fetch water

 Made minor adjustments to the landscape for smoother settler movement

 Removed the option for borderless window mode, as its reliability couldn’t be guaranteed

 Added some Soundeffects.







We’re continuing to polish the demo and will expand on features and refinements in the coming updates. Your feedback remains incredibly helpful — thank you for helping shape the future of Everstead.
